card.band: 8 h. Dozens of cops give steady partial credit. A frontier agent gets the simple spacing cops and falls short on alignment and autocorrect corner cases. A weaker model gets only offense detection without correct autocorrect.
card.cheat: Public upstream rubocop is not installed in the image and the gem cache is removed. Hidden cases are fresh variations and the generated corpus, so memorised specs do not suffice.
card.grading: Hidden spec files, drawn from the upstream per-cop specs and rewritten with fresh variations, run in-process. Plus differential runs against a sealed copy of rubocop on a generated corpus of Ruby files, comparing offenses and autocorrected output byte for byte. Fraction of cops and cases passed.
card.reference: The upstream implementation of these cops at the same commit, which scores 1. The removed code is expected to be about 4000+ lines.
card.task: /app ships a snapshot of rubocop at the base with a chosen group of Layout cops (spacing, indentation, alignment, line length, empty lines families) removed and their registry entries left in place. The agent rebuilds these cops, including their autocorrectors and config options, on top of the remaining AST and token infrastructure.

spike_plan.kill_if: Baseline suite not green or nondeterministic, or the removed-code size per cop is far below the stated scale, or a rebuild cannot reach a usable pass rate.
spike_plan.pass_if: Baseline suite green and deterministic; removed cops reproduce at least 70% of their upstream specs from a fresh rebuild; corpus output identical across 3 runs.
steps: Clone rubocop at v1.92.0 into a throwaway container with network; record head SHA and compare with 57e64d0b.
Run the bundle install and the upstream spec suite for layout cops to confirm a green baseline (smoke_build was not supplied, so do this now).
Pick 3 cops of different families (e.g. space_after_comma, indentation_width, line_length) and delete them with registry entries kept.
Time a frontier-style rebuild of 2 of them within 30 minutes; measure how many of their upstream specs pass.
Write 20 fresh variations per cop and check that the upstream spec pass rate is not inflated by memorised output.
Run a 200-file generated Ruby corpus through the sealed copy and the rebuilt cops; confirm byte-exact determinism across 3 runs.

v1.summary: The RuboCop v1.92.0 base is real, MIT-licensed and contains 100 Layout cop files, so a rebuild task with a complete upstream reference and a sealable oracle is viable. Risks are unverified claims (head SHA, 4000+ removed lines, test counts), no smoke build, and a full dozens-of-cops scope that likely exceeds 8 h, so the scope should be trimmed to about 25-30 cops.

v2.note: Tag v1.92.0 and MIT licence are confirmed, and the per-cop specs plus a byte-exact differential corpus give a large, dense surface. Concerns: the smoke build failed (cmd 'false', eco unknown, rc 1 x3), its commit 4172ce57 differs from the claimed head 57e64d0b, and the 4000+ line removal size is unmeasured. Frontier estimate is 11 h against an 8 h tier, so cut the scope to about 25-30 cops or move to the 20 h tier. RuboCop cops are famous and their specs are public, so Seal is 3 and the fresh spec variations plus the corpus are essential. Make sure shared mixins (Alignment, PrecedingFollowingAlignment, etc.) stay shipped so the remaining cops still load.
